caption_verbatim: Normal landmarks. Midsagittal a CT and b MR and coronal c CT and d MR. A Basion, B tuberculum sella, C basion (anterior margin of foramen magnum), D opisthion (posterior margin of foramen magnum), E posterior margin of the hard palate, F anterior arch of the atlas, G posterior arch of the atlas, H odontoid process, I body of the axis, J jugular tubercles, K occipital condyles, L lateral atlas masses
pointers: letter labels A-L: black letters on CT panels a,c; cream/yellow letters on MR panels b,d. Panel a: black arrows to A (frontonasal region), B (tuberculum sella), C (basion), D (opisthion), G (posterior arch C1); cream-yellow arrow F to anterior arch; cream-yellow bracket line E to posterior hard palate. Panel b: cream-yellow leader lines A,C,E,F; black arrows B,D,G. Panels c,d: letters only (H dens, I, J jugular tubercles, K condyles, L lateral masses). MISMATCH: caption says 'A Basion' but C is also basion and arrow A points to the anterior skull base/nasion region (printed caption error, probably nasion). Panel d letters differ from panel c: in d, I sits at top lateral and L sits below dens, whereas caption/panel c use I = body of axis and L = lateral atlas masses; in panel b L lies below H (axis body)

caption_verbatim: Normal lines and angles. a and b Chamberlain's line (tip of odontoid process and the anterior atlas arch lie below this line in both patients); c and d Wackenheim's clivus baseline (falls tangent to the posterior–superior corner of the odontoid process); e and f basal angle (average=134–135°); g and h clivus canal angle (minimum=150° in flexion maximum=180° in extension); i and j atlanto-occipital joint axis angle (average=124–127°)
pointers: drawn lines, cream/pale-yellow on radiographs and MR (a-h, j), black on coronal CT (i): a,b Chamberlain line hard palate to opisthion; c,d Wackenheim clivus baseline; e,f two-limb basal angle (nasion-sella-basion); g,h clivus-canal angle (clivus line plus posterior dens/axis body line); i,j two-limb atlanto-occipital joint axis angle on coronal CT/MR. No arrows, no letters in image other than panel letters a-j. No mismatch with caption; McGregor line and degree values are not drawn
modality: radiograph (lateral, a,c,e,g), MR (sagittal b,d,f,h; coronal j), CT (coronal i)

caption_verbatim: Basiocciput hypoplasia in four different patients. a Plain radiograph; b midsagittal CT scan; c and d midsagittal MR images. The hypoplastic basiocciput is indicated by the dots. The tip of the odontoid process and the anterior arch of C1 are well-above Chamberlain's line (solid lines) in all patients. The clivus canal angle (dotted lines) is abnormal in patients (a) and (c) [a=115°; b=125°; c=110°; d=135°)]. Note the Chiari I malformation and C2–3 nonsegmentation in (d)
pointers: black dots over hypoplastic basiocciput (a-d); thin light solid line (Chamberlain's) in each panel; light dotted lines (clivus-canal angle: Wackenheim line plus posterior vertebral body line) in each panel. No arrows. Angle values are not printed in the image. CAPTION INCONSISTENCY: text says clivus-canal angle abnormal in (a) and (c) only, yet b=125 and d=135 are also <150 (Table 2 cut-off)

caption_verbatim: Occipital condyle aplasia/hypoplasia with basiocciput hypoplasia in a 16-year-old male with neck pain (8/10), decreased gag, decreased tongue sensation, decreased hearing on the right and diffuse upper extremity hyperreflexia. He had previously undergone posterior fossa decompression. a Right parasagittal CT image shows complete absence of the occipital condyle. b Left parasagittal CT image demonstrates occipital condyle hypoplasia (arrow). c Coronal CT image confirms the findings of (a) and (b) and shows asymmetry of the atlanto-occipital joint axis angle and flattening of the skull base, the angle not able to be measured on this image. d Midsagittal T2-weighted MR image reveals the suboccipital craniectomy. There is evidence of platybasia (basal angle=150°) and severe basioccipital hypoplasia (dot). These all combine to produce severe basilar invagination, both the odontoid process and the anterior atlas arch (arrow) significantly above Chamberlain's line (extrapolated-solid line). e Midsagittal CT image. On this image, it is easier to appreciate the pseudoarthrosis of the anterior atlas arch with the undersurface of the hypoplastic basiocciput
pointers: black arrow (b) to hypoplastic condyle; letter label 'C1' black in a,b; cream-yellow dot on basiocciput (d); cream-yellow short line (d) at odontoid/anterior arch (caption 'arrow'); long cream-yellow line (d) = extrapolated Chamberlain line. Panels a,c,e have no overlay. Panel c: no angle drawn (consistent with caption)
topic: congenital (occipital condyle aplasia/hypoplasia, basiocciput hypoplasia, basilar invagination)
modality: CT (parasagittal, coronal, midsagittal), MR T2 sagittal

caption_verbatim: Occipital condyle hypoplasia in a 14-year-old male with occipital headaches and nasal speech with mild hyperreflexia and decreased lateral neck rotation to the right. a Right parasagittal CT demonstrates severe occipital condyle hypoplasia (arrow). b Left parasagittal CT reveals less severe condylar hypoplasia (arrow). c Coronal CT scan shows an atlanto-occipital joint axis angle of 140°. d and e Bilateral oblique 3D Vitrea images show the right lateral C1 mass (d-arrow) lies at a higher position than the left (e-arrow). f Right and g left parasagittal MR images also well-demonstrate the condylar hypoplasia (arrows). h Flexion midsagittal T2-weighted MR image demonstrates severe compression of the brainstem, a large cervical cord syringohydromyelic cavity, and platybasia with a basal angle of 170° (dotted angle). i Extension midsagittal T2-weighted MR image shows much less brainstem compression. Also note associated severe basioccipital hypoplasia (dot) and abnormal relationships of the odontoid tip and the anterior atlas arch in relation to Chamberlain's line (solid line) with severe basilar invagination. j Midsagittal CT image best demonstrates an abnormal Wackenheim's clivus baseline (dotted line) that does not even intersect the odontoid process. The clivus-canal angle (arrow) is markedly abnormal at 90°
pointers: black arrows a,b (condyle); black letters C1; cream-yellow two-limb angle lines c (AO joint axis angle); black arrows d,e (lateral C1 mass, 3D); cream-yellow arrows f,g (condyle, MR); white dotted lines h (basal angle); cream-yellow dot and long cream-yellow line i (basioccipital hypoplasia dot; Chamberlain line); white dotted line (Wackenheim) plus cream-yellow solid line plus cream-yellow arrow j (clivus-canal angle). Matches caption; angle values not printed in image
topic: congenital (occipital condyle hypoplasia, platybasia, basilar invagination)
modality: CT (parasagittal, coronal, 3D VRT, midsagittal), MR T2 sagittal flexion/extension

caption_verbatim: Basiocciput hypoplasia and bilateral occipital condylar hypoplasia in an 18-year-old female with headache. She had mild bilateral decreased gag and mild diffuse hyperreflexia on physical examination. a Right and b left parasagittal CT images demonstrate mild, symmetric occipital condyle hypoplasia (arrows). c Coronal CT image also demonstrates the hypoplasia. Note that the atlanto-occipital joint axis angle remains within normal range (angle). d Midsagittal CT image reveals associated severe basioccipital hypoplasia. e Midsagittal T2-weighted MR image demonstrates basilar invagination (Chamberlain's line is drawn) and a cervical cord syringohydromyelic cavity
pointers: black arrows a,b (condyles); black letters C1; cream-yellow two-limb angle lines c (AO joint axis angle; lines are cream-yellow, not black); cream-yellow Chamberlain line e; panel d no overlay. Verified at full resolution
topic: congenital (basiocciput and condylar hypoplasia, basilar invagination, syrinx)

caption_verbatim: Partial atlanto-occipital non-segmentation in an adult female with broad-based gait, numbness and tingling in the hands, and constant occipital headache. On physical examination, she had a positive gag reflex, diffuse hyperreflexia, decreased touch and pinprick below the neck, and bilateral lateral gaze nystagmus. (a) Midsagittal CT image demonstrates posterior atlanto-occipital non-segmentation (arrow), atlanto-axial subluxation with widening of the anterior atlantodental interval (double arrow) and basilar invagination, both the odontoid and the anterior atlas arch above Chamberlain's line (extrapolated-solid line). Wackenheim's clivus baseline (dotted line) abnormally intersects the odontoid process. b Right and c left parasagittal and d coronal CT images reveal complete non-segmentation of the lateral atlas masses. e Midsagittal, f coronal, g right oblique, and h left oblique 3D Vitrea reconstructed images optimally reveal the non-segmentation and the atlanto-axial subluxation with severe compromise of the osseous foramen magnum. i Midsagittal T1-weighted MR image demonstrates the severe resultant compression of the CMJ, tonsillar ectopia, and a small cervical cord syrinx cavity or area of myelomalacia (arrow)
pointers: cream-yellow arrow at posterior atlanto-occipital fusion (a); cream-yellow double-headed arrow = anterior atlantodental interval (a); long cream-yellow solid line = extrapolated Chamberlain line (a); white/cream dotted line = Wackenheim baseline (a); black arrow (i) at cord. Panels b-h without overlay. Matches caption.
topic: congenital (partial atlanto-occipital non-segmentation, AAS, basilar invagination)
modality: CT (sagittal, coronal), 3D VRT, MR T1 sagittal

Note narrowing of the anterior–posterior dimension of the spinal canal at the C1 level. c Midsagittal and d axial 3D Vitrea reconstructed images demonstrate the relationships and narrowing of the osseous cervical spinal canal. e Midsagittal MR image best reveals the compression of the posterior aspect of the spinal cord at the C1 ring level (arrow)

Also note the posterior arch rachischisis making this a split atlas

caption_verbatim: Split atlas. a Lateral radiograph demonstrates the configuration of a normal anterior atlas arch with well-corticated margins (short arrows). A very small (normal) anterior atlantodental interval is defined (long arrow). b Lateral radiograph demonstrates a rounded, hypertrophic anterior atlas arch without typical cortication (arrows). This anterior arch overlaps the odontoid process such that an anterior atlantodental interval cannot be assessed. c Midsagittal T1-weighted MR image shows the typical, rounded low signal intensity of the midline fibrous tissue in the rachischisis (dot)

caption_verbatim: Os odontoideum in a 20-year-old male with numbness and tingling on the left, "hot flashes," and decreased temperature at night. He was grossly hyperreflexic and had clonus in all four extremities. a Flexion and (b) extension lateral radiographs demonstrate severe instability. The os is not identifiable on these radiographs. Wackenheim's clivus baseline is indicated by the black lines. Note the marked narrowing of the spinal canal at the C1 level in flexion that reduces in extension (double arrows). There is a very rounded, hypertrophic appearance to the anterior arch of the atlas (dots) that should be an indication that this is an os odontoideum and not a type II odontoid fracture. c Flexion midsagittal T2-weighted MR image in a different patient demonstrates severe spinal cord compression and pathologic T2 signal within the cord (black arrow). The anterior arch of the atlas (white arrow) maintains a normal relationship with the os (white dot). d Midsagittal and e coronal CT images best demonstrate the osseous relationships. Note the well-corticated upper margin of the axis body in (e) which would not be consistent with a type II odontoid fracture
pointers: black lines (a,b) Wackenheim baseline; yellow double-headed arrows (a,b) spinal canal narrowing at C1; black dots with white ring on anterior arch (a,b); yellow arrow (c) at anterior arch (caption says white arrow); yellow dot on os (c); black arrow (c) at cord compression. d,e no overlay.
topic: congenital (os odontoideum, instability); trauma mimic (type II dens fracture)
modality: radiograph (lateral flexion/extension), MR T2 sagittal flexion, CT sagittal/coronal

The anterior atlas arch does not demonstrate the normal corticated crescentic configuration as it is rotated, appearing "fat" (b-arrow). c Axial CT scan at the level of the nasopharynx reveals a suppurative medial retropharyngeal node (arrow). d Axial CT image at the level of the anterior arch of the atlas demonstrates rotary atlantoaxial subluxation. Also note the prevertebral space widening (double arrow)
pointers: a no overlay; b: black arrow (anterior arch) and three cream-yellow double-headed arrows (prevertebral soft tissue widening); c: black arrow (retropharyngeal node); d: cream-yellow double-headed arrow (prevertebral widening). Verified

caption_verbatim: Osteogenesis imperfecta, type IV, in an 18-year-old female with an 18-month history of progressive headache, left hand numbness, clumsy hands bilaterally, and 6 months of urinary incontinence. The tip of the odontoid is 35 mm above Chamberlain's line (dotted line), and there is severe platybasia with the basal angle (solid lines) measuring 160°. The clivus canal angle (dashed lines) measures 75°. Note the large syringohydromyelic cavity with vertebral scalloping. b Axial T2-weighted MR image shows the odontoid and lateral C1 masses (dots) at the level of the inner ear structures (arrows)
pointers: a: cream-yellow solid two-limb line (basal angle), white dotted line palate to opisthion region (Chamberlain), cream/black dashed lines (clivus-canal angle); b: cream-yellow arrows (inner ear structures) and cream/white dots (odontoid, C1 masses). Values 160/75/35 mm are caption-only, not printed. Verified
